claims.text: Local chemical environments govern the reliable formation of noble metal-based high-entropy alloy nanomaterials.
Electronic structures govern the reliable formation of noble metal-based high-entropy alloy nanomaterials.
Local chemical environments influence the catalytic activity and selectivity of noble metal-based high-entropy alloy nanomaterials.
Electronic structures influence the catalytic activity and selectivity of noble metal-based high-entropy alloy nanomaterials.
Operando X-ray absorption spectroscopy can elucidate the relevant local chemical environments and electronic structures.
Catalytic performance will correlate positively with local chemical environments and electronic structures characterized as optimal by operando X-ray absorption spectroscopy.
The proposed relationship is expected to hold for catalytic reactions including hydrogen evolution and oxygen reduction.
The proposed relationship may not apply to other types of catalytic reactions.
The exact relationships among composition, structure, and catalytic activity remain unclear.
